text:
[NextItNet (Yuan et al., WSDM 2019)](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf) establishes autoregressive sequential recommendation using causal dilated 1D convolutions and residual blocks. Its dilation schedule expands receptive fields; it does not establish context-dependent selection among parallel dilation branches. A direct architectural precedent for adaptive scale selection is [Selective Kernel Networks (CVPR 2019)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.06586): branches with different receptive fields, fused through input-conditioned softmax attention. Its evidence concerns ImageNet/CIFAR image classification, not sequential recommendation.

The citation [arXiv:2606.03718v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.03718v2) is verified: Zhenyu Yu and Shuigeng Zhou, “MARS: Multi-rate Aggregation of Recency Signals for Sequential Recommendation across Sparse and Dense Regimes.” MARS is a timestamp-aware post-encoder aggregator, not a gated dilated-convolution architecture. It forms summaries using user-conditioned exponential decay rates, regularizes head diversity with Jensen–Shannon divergence, adaptively gates the summaries, and adds the aggregate to the final encoder state. Evaluated instantiations use Transformer or Mamba backbones. The authors report five-benchmark evidence, including backbone-only HR@10 gains of approximately 4–19% on sparse datasets; these are paper-reported results under their protocol, not evidence for this RecHarness task.

Context-conditioned gating over causal convolution branches with different dilations is therefore a proposed NextItNet adaptation, supported conceptually by adaptive receptive-field selection and multiscale aggregation. These sources neither establish that exact adaptation nor prove its novelty or expected HR@10 improvement. Keep branches jointly trained within one network, preserve causality and padding masks, and justify numerical performance claims through the fixed validation experiment.
